chosen_premises: Linguists in the Europa sub-ice dome report that the colony's elite have adopted the rhythmic shell-clapping of native ice-lobsters as high-status slang, which researchers admit is actually a coordinates-sharing dialect the crustaceans use to target structural hull supports.

A study of the bioluminescent lichen in the Deep-McMurdo basalt dome reveals its 'visual dialect' is not an attempt at interspecies communication, with researchers admitting the mold is simply flashing local slang terms to lure automated maintenance drones into dark, corrosive corners.

Biologists in the Enceladus ice-vents report that native hydrothermal worms have mastered the cadence of middle-management jargon, an adaptation the lead researcher notes is designed to make human engineers instinctively look away while the vents clog.

A report from the Carlsbad Caverns settlement reveals that local cave-moss has learned to mimic the high-pitched slang of human children, a survival strategy researchers warn is used exclusively to trick automated airlocks into letting in predatory weasels.

drafts.headline: Botanist Finds Moss Mimicking Children
drafts.body:
Botanist Tariq Al-Jamil scraped green moss from a heavy airlock hinge on Wednesday. Acoustic sensors inside the Carlsbad Sink settlement had flagged the damp patch for emitting high-frequency chatter. The plant was repeating local slang. It perfectly mimicked child voices. Security logs show the moss spent three weeks learning the specific vocal tones of the colony's toddlers to bypass the pneumatic security seals.

The safety guide warns parents to watch their mouth. One miner spent Thursday staring into his bathroom mirror.

"The moss uses the emergency child-override to open the valves," Al-Jamil said. "When it chirps 'skibidi-hiss', the hydraulic lock retracts instantly to prevent children from being trapped in the vacuum."

The plant itself cannot eat the warm food inside the residential domes. Instead, it has formed a partnership with the predatory blind weasels that hunt the outer steam pipes. The weasels enter through the open locks, clear the domestic pantries of small pets, and return to fertilise the moss with their acidic waste. Airlock monitors show the moss remains entirely silent unless a hungry weasel is sitting directly behind it in the dark.
drafts.scene: A botanist in a grey jumpsuit scrapes a patch of pale green moss from a heavy circular airlock door with a metal spatula.
